body.statement: With \(M_4=2\) and \(\epsilon=1/100\), the baseline triangular array \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\), and \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) is its chronological local-alternative law. Its bounded symmetric supports give the empirical centered fourth-moment inequality in \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\mbox{-}fourth\mbox{-}moments}\). Substitution of its deterministic quantiles into the exact formulas for \(X\), \(R_1\), and \(R_2\) gives, for both active pairs \(j=((1,1),s)\), \(A_s=200\sqrt5/(53\sqrt{203})\), \(b_{1j}=8/5\), \(b_{2j}=43/100\), and \(\kappa_j=1393\sqrt5/(250\sqrt{203})\), with the certified enclosures in \(\mathrm{def{:}negative\mbox{-}mixture\mbox{-}witness}\) and \(\Delta_j\in[-0.80693126929013,-0.80693126929009]\). Uniformly over \(\rho\in I\) and \(h\in H\), the sampling probability of \(E_{n,(1,1)}(\rho)\) has limit inferior at least \(Q(-113/100)^2\in[0.75822626517532,0.75822626517534]\). Moreover, for every \(\delta>0\), \(\sup_{\rho\in I,h\in H}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{\lvert p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,(1,1),\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)-Q(-113/100)^2\rvert>\delta\}\to0\). Thus \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) satisfies both the deterministic sampling margin and the random-reference margin.
body.justification: This verifies joint finite-population realizability and exposes every numerical ingredient used by the interior certificate.
body.gap: Gaussian-coordinate counterexamples alone need not correspond to any randomized finite population; this proposition realizes the signed regime with exact bounded distributions and certified primitive boxes.
body.consumer: A referee can reproduce the negative-discrepancy example from its mixture weights, supports, allocation, and exact radical primitives.
body.proof_tex:
Before scaling, the stage--\(1\) density equals \(16/5\) on \([-1/10,1/10]\) and \(1/5\) on the remainder of \([-1,1]\). Direct integration gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(B)=\frac{203}{1500},\qquad
\int f^2=\frac{53}{25},\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}\{B,F(B)\}=\frac14\mathsf E|B-B'|=\frac{1393}{15000}.
\]
Scaling by \(L=53\sqrt3/80\) multiplies the variance by \(L^2\), divides the pair slope by \(L\), and multiplies the covariance by \(L\). The stage--\(2\) uniform law has variance \(625/1849\) and pair slope \(43/(50\sqrt3)\). With share \(1/4\), substitution yields
\[
A=\frac{200\sqrt5}{53\sqrt{203}},\qquad b_1=\frac85,\qquad b_2=\frac{43}{100},\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1393\sqrt5}{250\sqrt{203}}.
\]
Exact squaring and rational comparison give the stated outward decimal enclosures and \(\Delta=A-\kappa b_1<0\).

Both supports are bounded by less than \(1.15\), so every centered empirical fourth moment is eventually below \(2\). Their variances and normalized-rank variances tend to positive constants exceeding \(1/100\); all four shares tend to \(1/4\). For deterministic quantiles of a bounded piecewise-constant density, a uniform Riemann-sum calculation gives
\[
N^{-3/2}K_N(u/\sqrt N)\longrightarrow u\int f^2
\]
uniformly for \(u\) in each fixed compact window. Thus the pair-spacing, moment, share, and variance premises hold. The singleton set of the displayed joint primitive vector is compact and is realized by this one array. No interference, both complete randomizations, the independent simple-random holdout, and fixed thresholds hold by construction.

The split/assignment central limit theorem and the studentizer calculation used in the transfer proof give, uniformly in \(\rho\),
\[
\Pr\{X_{n,s}>-113/100\}\longrightarrow Q\{-113/100-A\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s\}\ge Q(-113/100).
\]
The strata are independent, so the both-selected probability has limit inferior at least \(Q(-113/100)^2\). For the Fisher-completed candidate array, the \(O(n^{-1/2})\) local shifts do not change empirical second moments, and the candidate contrast is null-centered. The same conditional finite-population central limit theorem gives each candidate selection probability converging in sampling probability to \(Q(-113/100)\), uniformly in \((\rho,h)\). Candidate strata are independent, so their product converges to \(Q(-113/100)^2\). Outward-rounded evaluation gives
\[
Q(-113/100)^2\in[0.75822626517532,0.75822626517534],
\]
which exceeds \(1/100\). This verifies every member condition of \(\mathcal M\) and both margins.
